en: The Sūtra on the Questions of the Brahmāṇa Dīrghanakha, translated by the Tripitaka Master Yijing of the Great Tang, under imperial decree.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha.

He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, as well as other bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, kings, ministers, śramaṇas, brahmins, and followers of external paths, along with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and non-humans, all of whom stood gazing up at him in reverence.

At that time, the World-Honored One expounded for them the subtle Dharma of his own realization—namely, that which is excellent in the beginning, middle, and end; skillful in both phrasing and meaning; pure, complete, and pristine; the very characteristic of the holy life (brahmacarya).
At that time, there was a brahmin with long nails who came to where the Buddha was, stood leaning on his staff, and asked:
"Gautama! Have you truly declared such things as this: 'The world is produced by one's own karma; karma is the giver, karma is the place of birth, karma is one's kinsman, and karma is one's refuge'?"
The Buddha told the brahmin:
“I declare that the world is conditioned by one’s own karma; karma is the giver, karma is the place of birth, karma is one’s kin, and karma is one’s refuge.”
The brāhmaṇa said: "If that is so, Śramaṇa Gautama!
What karma did you perform previously that caused you to obtain this vajra-like, indestructible, and solid body?"
The Buddha told the brahmin:
"In a previous life, I distanced myself from taking the life-force of sentient beings; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit."
“Śramaṇa Gautama! What karma did you perform in the past that caused you to obtain the marks of long, slender fingers and webbed hands?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:
"In a previous life, I abstained from stealing the property of others; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit.
"Śramaṇa Gautama!"
“What karma did you previously perform that caused you to obtain such perfect physical strength and the full maturity of your faculties?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:
“In a previous life, I remained far removed from the defilement of desire for women; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit.”
“Śramaṇa Gautama! What karma did you perform in the past that caused you to obtain such a broad and long tongue, capable of covering your own face?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:
“In a previous life, I abstained from false speech and deceiving others; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit.
“O Śramaṇa Gautama! [he said.]
“What karma did you previously perform to cause you to obtain such majestic and dignified deportment, walking with the gait of a lion?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:
“In a previous life, I stayed far away from all intoxicants and places of heedlessness; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit.”
“Śramaṇa Gautama! What karma did you perform in the past that has caused you to obtain a body adorned with such subtle and wondrous marks and signs?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:
"In a previous life, I abstained from singing, dancing, and the company of courtesans; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit.
"O Śramaṇa Gautama!"
"What karma did you perform previously that caused you to obtain this most excellent fragrance, which perfumes your body?
The Buddha told the brahmin:
"In a former life, I remained far removed from the adornment of incense, flowers, and garlands; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit."
“Śramaṇa Gautama! What karma did you perform in the past that has caused you to obtain and enjoy this most excellent and sublime diamond throne?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:
“In a previous life, I abstained from high beds, large beds, and all things that foster arrogance; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit.
“O Śramaṇa Gautama! [he said.]
"What karma did you previously perform that caused you to obtain forty teeth that are fresh white, even, and level?
The Buddha told the brahmin:
"In a previous life, I abstained from eating and drinking at improper times; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit."
“Śramaṇa Gautama! What karma did you perform in the past that caused you to obtain this perfectly beautiful uṣṇīṣa on the crown of your head?
The Buddha told the brāhmaṇa:

"In a previous life, toward the Triple Gem, the two teachers—the śramaṇa and the brāhmaṇa—my parents, my elders, and those worthy of reverence, I prostrated with my five limbs touching the ground, offering worship with sincere devotion and a mind free from pride; by the power of that karma, I have now obtained this fruit."
At that time, the brahmin, seeing that the Buddha had explained for him how cause and effect are not in vain, said:
"Gautama! What is the name of this merit?"
"How should one receive and uphold it?
The Buddha said:

"This is called the eightfold pure precept (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*). If one can receive and uphold them from a teacher for even one day and one night, or for a longer period, the fruit obtained will be such as this."

At that time, the brahmin Dīrghanakha, having heard from the Buddha the teaching on the eightfold pure precepts of the day and night—which, by virtue of having previously distanced oneself from base and evil deeds, enables one to attain sublime adornment—received them with deep faith and joy, leaping for gladness.
Immediately before the Buddha, he cast aside his arrogance, threw his staff upon the ground, joined his palms in reverence, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and said:
“World-Honored One!
Only now do I realize that the retribution for the karma of good and evil is not in vain.
From this day forth until the end of my life, I take refuge in the Buddha, the most honored among two-legged beings;
until the end of my life, I take refuge in the Dharma, the most honored among those free from desire.
For as long as life shall last, I take refuge in the Saṅgha, the most venerable among all assemblies.
I undertake the eightfold Upavāsa pure precepts, from this very moment until the rising of the sun tomorrow morning; during that interval:
"I shall not harm any living being, nor shall I steal the property of others."
Abstaining from sexual misconduct and false speech, From drinking intoxicants and occasions of heedlessness,
From perfumes, ornaments, dancing, and singing, From high beds and eating at improper times—
I now distance myself from all these; I uphold the pure eightfold precepts.
The second and third times he spoke likewise.
The Buddha said to the brahmin:
“Excellent!”
"Excellent!
It should be practiced in this way; it should be upheld in this way.

When the World-Honored One had spoken these teachings, the brahmin, the assembly of bhikṣus, and all the humans, devas, and others were filled with great joy, and they faithfully accepted and practiced them.
The Sūtra on the Questions of the Brahmacārin Dīrghanakha (The Long-Nail Brahmin)
